title: BCIT Basic Guard Duty
description: EEG dataset from the Basic Guard Duty study of the Brain-Computer Interaction Technologies (BCIT) collection, designed to measure sustained vigilance in a realistic setting. Participants verified replica ID cards against reference face photographs at varying queuing rates while 256-channel BioSemi EEG and eye tracking were recorded. The dataset is formatted in BIDS with HED annotations and accompanies companion calibration and baseline driving datasets.
methods_description: Participants completed ten 5-minute guard duty blocks, deciding whether to allow or deny access based on ID-photo pairings presented at stochastic queue rates of 1 to 25 per minute. EEG was recorded with BioSemi 256 (+8) channel systems at 1024 Hz, including 4 eye and 2 mastoid channels, alongside SMI REDEYE250 eye tracking. The task was performed in conjunction with driving simulator tasks whose data are not included here.
